classification.habitat: Dry scrub, open woodland, roadsides and hedges
classification.distribution: Indian subcontinent and tropical regions where cultivated or naturalised

identification.description: Erect spiny shrub with opposite leaves, axillary spines and conspicuous yellow flowers.
identification.whole_plant: Much-branched shrub, generally erect and armed with spines.
identification.stem: Young branches green to brown with paired axillary spines; older branches become woody.
identification.leaf: Opposite, simple, elliptic to lanceolate leaves with entire margins.
identification.flower: Bright yellow, tubular flowers borne in axillary clusters; flowering is conspicuous.
identification.seed: Usually two seeds per capsule, flattened and adapted for dispersal.

therapeutics.precautions: Spines can cause injury during collection; use authenticated material and appropriate references.

major_constituents: Iridoid glycosides and flavonoid/phenolic constituents have been reported

modern_information.evidence_summary: Barleria prionitis has been investigated experimentally for anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antimicrobial-related activities. These findings are not presented as established clinical efficacy.
modern_information.safety_notes: Handle carefully because of spines; use authenticated plant material.

student.quick_revision: Sairayak (Barleria prionitis): spiny Acanthaceae shrub with opposite leaves, axillary spines and yellow tubular flowers.

teaching_points: Demonstrate paired axillary spines and opposite leaves.
Use flowering material for rapid field identification.
practical_points: Inspect flower tube and capsule characters.

doctor.quick_reference: Sairayak is traditionally used in selected Vata-related indications; botanical identity and plant part should be confirmed before use.
key_precautions: Use verified references for dosing and contraindications
